(b) The CP1500AVRLCD3 manual (same shortened wording as LX1) lists E02/E11/E21/E22 and DROPS E01 entirely, while the LX G3 manual and every earlier CP manual keep E01. So on these newer models the technician must expect 4 codes, not 5.

brands.notes: US/Finnish power-quality maker; no eaton.com/pk country site, but Eaton UPS is actively sold and serviced in Pakistan through authorised distributors (Greaves Pakistan, BroadPeak International) and IT retailers such as Toprated Lahore.

series.name: 5P Gen2 (line-interactive UPS, tower and rack models 550-3000 VA class)
series.notes: Generation 2 of the 5P line-interactive family. No numeric A/F codes in the manual - named LCD conditions with LED colour/on-off and beeper cadence. Differences from gen-1 5P (SERIES 4): overload threshold is '>100% of nominal' here vs '>105%' in gen 1; 'End of battery life' is renamed 'Battery fault'; overtemperature now says the UPS 'shuts down' if temperature rises another 10 degrees C (gen 1 9PX wording says 'transfers to Bypass mode or shuts down if Bypass is unusable'); RPO is a separate named cause. Treat gen 1 and gen 2 as separate lookups.

series.name: 5P 650-1550 i (line-interactive UPS, tower/rack/wall)
series.notes: Line-interactive family. The gen-1 5P manual does NOT publish numeric A/F codes - it uses a short 'Operation status' text table that the LCD shows. Do not merge with SERIES 5 (5P Gen2) or with the 9PX table: 5P Gen2 adds explicit LED colours and beeper cadences and renames 'End of battery life' as 'Battery fault'.

series.name: 93E 15-80 kVA (3-phase online UPS, 380/400/415 V)
series.notes: The 93E 15-80 kVA manual publishes NO numeric A/F fault codes. It documents the MIMIC status-indicator LED table (Table 6-1), the system-event horn behaviour (para 6.2.2) and the typical status messages (Table 6-5). Actual per-alarm text lives in the Events/History log on the LCD and in the network card's alarm log, neither of which is published as a static table in this manual - see NEGATIVE. Do NOT assume the 9E A/F codes apply to a 93E. Same Table 6-1 wording is repeated in the Eaton 93E 300-500 kVA manual (https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/products/backup-power-ups-surge-it-power-distribution/au-products/eaton-93e/93E_300-500kVA_user_manual_EN.pdf), so it is treated as one family here. The same MIMIC panel is used across 93E / 93PM / 93PS, but only 93E is in scope for this KB.

series.name: 9E 1-3 kVA (online UPS 1-3kVA + 9E EBM)
series.notes: Do NOT merge with SERIES 1. Same brand, same letter scheme, different code set: 1-3kVA has no A007/A10A/A806/A802/AC20 but adds A502/A604/A612, F007/F308/F500/F806/F208/F613/F816. F004 is worded differently ('Inner temperature high' in the minor-fault table, 'UPS Over temperature fault' in the major table). A107 is worded differently ('Cable connection error (Input Line and Neutral inversion)'). A60D is 'Battery not connected' here vs 'Batteries missing or Battery Box missing or not connected' on 6-20kVA. F302/F303 = 'DC Bus too low' and F300/F301 = 'DC Bus too high' here, vs 'Capacitor bank under/overvoltage' on 6-20kVA.

series.name: 9E 6-20 kVA (online UPS 6-20kVA, 3:1 and 1:1)
series.notes: The only Eaton small-UPS family with a full numeric A/F code table in the manual. Applies ONLY to 6-20 kVA. The 9E 1-3kVA manual has a DIFFERENT and partly conflicting code set (e.g. it has F007/F500/F308/F806/F208/F613/F816 but no A007/A10A/A806/A802/AC20) - see series eaton-9e-1-3k and CONFLICTS. F304 also differs in wording: 'Unbalanced capacitor bank' here vs 'DC Bus unbalanced' on 1-3kVA.

series.name: 9PX / 9PX Gen2 (online UPS 700VA-11kVA)
series.notes: The 9PX family does NOT use numeric A/F codes in the manual; it uses named LCD conditions with LED + beeper patterns, and separate Event log / Fault log lists on the front panel. Second source: Eaton 9PX Gen2 5-11 kVA Advanced user manual (https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/products/backup-power-ups-surge-it-power-distribution/backup-power-ups/eaton-9px-gen2-emea/9px-gen2-resources-emea/eaton-9px-5-11-kva-gen2-advanced-user-manual-en-us.pdf) reproduces the same 11 conditions; the only difference found is UPS overtemperature, which the Gen2 manual gives as 'Beep continuous' instead of '1 beep every 3 seconds'. Do NOT reuse 9E A/F codes for a 9PX.

series.name: Ellipse PRO 650/850/1200/1600 VA (line-interactive UPS, AVR)
series.notes: Smallest UPS in the Eaton line. The manual publishes NO numeric fault codes at all - diagnosis is by numbered LCD icon (6 = ON/OFF button, 8 = ASR LED, 12 = Internal fault, 18 = Surge protection outlets, 19 = Battery backup outlets, 20 = Protection circuit breaker) plus the numbered Problem/Diagnostic/Solution table. The 'Internal fault' LCD icon 12 is the closest thing to a fault code. Do NOT merge with the 5P/5P Gen2 tables: those use different LED names and different wording. This manual is multi-language in one PDF; the entries below come from the ENGLISH section (pages 6-9).

brands.name: Felicity Solar
brands.notes: Official name Guangzhou Felicity Solar Technology Co., Ltd. (trading style Felicitysolar / FelicityESS), based in Guangzhou, China - the AU in the brief template is unsupported by any source. Pakistan presence CONFIRMED: dedicated /pk/ market site, /pk/become-distributors/ channel page, and a dated news item about a first product seminar in Pakistan with an agent certification ceremony; the PK-focused SKUs are the IVGM inverter series and the FLA battery series, both covered below. No consolidated fault-code table exists on the vendor website - codes live only in per-model PDF manuals.

series.name: FLA12100 LiFePO4 battery pack
series.notes: This is the FLA battery series Felicitysolar showcased at its first Pakistan product seminar, so it is high-relevance for the AC Ustad KB. The manual's 4.3 LED table documents 14 LED fault patterns C01-C14 but only C14 is tied to a named condition ('C14 Output loss') in the extractable text. The remaining C01-C13 patterns are recorded in NEGATIVE rather than guessed, because the manual does not state their meanings in a readable form. FAULT mode = red LED ON, green LED OFF, four SOC LEDs showing the code.

series.name: IVCM PRO Series 1kW~3kW hybrid inverter/charger
series.notes: 12 V/24 V small hybrid inverter/charger. Warning = Fault LED flashing + buzzer beeping; fault = Fault LED solid. Several rows in the source table have NO extractable code number (the number column is vector-outlined in the CDR-derived PDF) and are therefore NOT transcribed here - see NEGATIVE. Sibling manual 358-010428-00 prints a similar table but its number column is ambiguous, so it was used only as a weak cross-check, not to assign codes.

series.name: IVEM Series 3kVA~5kVA hybrid inverter/charger
series.notes: 48 V hybrid inverter/charger, up to 12 units in parallel. NOTE the code-string collision with SERIES 2: here 51 = 'BMS does not allow inverter to CHARGE battery' and 52 = 'BMS does not allow inverter to DISCHARGE battery', which is the OPPOSITE assignment to the IVGM table. Always read the model. Codes 1-26, 30-39, 47-49, 55-79 and 81+ in the fault table have no extractable code number in the source PDF and are NOT transcribed - see NEGATIVE.

series.name: IVGM4K6/5K/6K LP1G1 hybrid inverter
series.notes: Pakistan launch SKU. Warning table (ch.8) and fault table (ch.9) reuse identical numeric strings with DIFFERENT meanings - always read whether the manual called it a warning or a fault. Cross-checked against the Apollo-4K6/5K6LP1G01-MX guide (doc 358-S010018-00) which prints a byte-identical code table; not duplicated here. Codes 03, 05, 08, 09, 12, 13, 18, 27, 32, 37, 41, 55-82, 84-86, 88+ are absent from the printed table.

series.name: LUX-S-1600LG01 Micro Energy Storage System
series.notes: Combined lithium battery + inverter unit, 32 V battery, 60 A max charge current, max PV 95 V, MPPT 30 A. Table 8.10 codes 1-22; 14-20 and 22 could not be read from the source PDF. The manual's own troubleshooting chapter is explicit that many of these indications are normal protection behaviour, not a product fault - do not over-react to them.

series.name: T-REX-10KLP3G01 three-phase hybrid inverter
series.notes: The code table of this model is unreadable in the source PDF (CorelDRAW-to-PDF conversion outlined the text), so only the two codes actually recovered are listed. Codes 01-24 and 26+ of the chapter 9 table remain unverified and are in NEGATIVE. A reseller transcription (felicitysolar.me) claims 48 codes for this model; it was NOT used as a source. IMPORTANT: on this model fault = LED always-on AND buzzer continuous, warning = LED flashing AND buzzer intermittent - a different LED rule from SERIES 1.

series.name: T-REX 25/30/40/50 KHP3G01 three-phase hybrid inverter
series.notes: Three-phase commercial hybrid. Warning table = codes 01-22 (17 not used), unit keeps running. Fault table = codes 01-94, output is cut. Codes 80-86, 89, 90, 95 are not present in the printed table. Parallel CAN comms codes (87/88) and BMS comms codes (92/93) only appear on units fitted with the parallel/BMS option. Do NOT merge with Series 8 (T-REX-10KLP3G01) - different table, different numbering.

brands.name: FoxESS
brands.notes: Chinese-origin solar hybrid inverter maker that runs per-country manual portals; pk.fox-ess.com hosts the manuals that apply to Pakistani installs, confirming active PK distribution.

series.name: H1(G2)/AC1(G2) - battery and EPS faults
series.notes: Battery-facing alarms. The Buck and Boost entries are MOSFET stage failures and are workshop items, not site items. CORRECTION to an earlier draft: the H1 V1.6 table DOES list both 'Bat Relay Open' and 'Bat Relay Short Circuit' (p.42) - an earlier claim that they were KH/KA-and-H3-only was wrong and has been removed. They are not expanded as separate entries here only because of the code-count budget; the verified strings are 'The battery relay keeps open' and 'The battery relay keeps close', both with the same disconnect/reconnect remedy, and both appear on H1, KH/KA and H3.

series.name: H1(G2)/AC1(G2) - BMS, battery-pack and meter communication faults
series.notes: The four rows where FoxESS's own remedy is to fix a CABLE rather than a part, plus the meter's equivalent. These are the highest-yield codes in Pakistan because cheap multi-pack ECS installs with mixed batches and loosely seated comms leads produce them constantly. The remaining 17 Bms* rows in the same H1 table all carry the identical remedy 'Please contact battery supplier' and are deliberately NOT expanded here (see foxess-kh-ka-bms-mismatch for the 'Unmatch' family, which is the subset a technician can actually act on). Verified present on H1 V1.6 AND on KH/KA (both copies) AND on H3 V1.0.4 - but kept as separate series because the KH/KA and H3 tables differ in other rows.

series.name: H1(G2)/AC1(G2) - output current, DC bus and PV input current
series.notes: The SW/HW prefix pair is FoxESS's software-detected vs hardware-detected twin. Both have the SAME official remedy (disconnect PV, grid and battery, then reconnect), so they are kept as separate codes but must not be given different field advice. Earlier E1 manuals print the strings WITHOUT the 'Fault' suffix (e.g. 'HW Inv Cur', 'SW Bus Vol') - treat those as aliases, not different codes.

series.name: H1(G2)/AC1(G2) - grid and AC monitoring faults
series.notes: Single-phase hybrid, FoxCloud/app-driven. Strings are named text exactly as printed on the LCD. Do NOT merge with foxess-t-series-grid 'Grid volt fault' (different spelling, different remedy) or with the R-series 4-digit numerics. Verified against the full H1 V1.6 table: this exact four-row grid block is byte-identical on H1 G2, KH/KA and H3 - the codes are shared but the SERIES are kept separate because other rows in the same tables differ.

series.name: H1(G2)/AC1(G2) - insulation, residual current and earth faults
series.notes: Insulation/leakage family, all four rows sit together in the H1 V1.6 table between the PV-current and temperature rows. The manual's own remedy for all four is identical and weak (check wire insulation, wait, seek help) - the concrete steps below are field practice built around FoxESS's stated check, not invented FoxESS text. CRITICAL: 'Iso Fault' here is an insulation-DAMAGE inspection. The T-series 'ISO fault' is a measured-impedance test (should be > 100 kOhm) and the R-series 1124 is a two-step impedance check with an APP setting. Three different official remedies for the same word - never merge. The H1 manual also states, in section 6, that an earth-fault alarm shows as 'Isolation fault' on screen with the RED LED lit.

series.name: H3/AC3 (three-phase hybrid) - grid and phase-synchronising faults
series.notes: H3/AC3 models verified in the manual's own model list: H3-5.0-E, H3-6.0-E, H3-8.0-E, H3-9.9-E, H3-10.0-E, H3-12.0-E. Four of these five grid rows are byte-identical to H1 G2 and KH/KA - they are still kept in a SEPARATE series because PLL_ OverTime exists only on the three-phase line and because a three-phase Pakistani install must be told to check all three phases, not one. Never merge into foxess-h1-ac1-g2-grid even though 'Grid Volt Fault' is the same string.

series.name: H3/AC3 (three-phase hybrid) - power stage, bus and relay faults
series.notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT MODEL-LINE BLOCK IN THIS FILE. Every code here is a string that also exists on H1/KH-KA, but on H3 the OFFICIAL REMEDY IS DIFFERENT. Verified by reading the two tables side by side: (a) H3's 'SW Bus Vol Fault' adds 'Please check whether the N line is connected to the GRID port of the inverter' and 'at least ensure that the master is upgraded to 1.69 or above' - H1 V1.6 has neither. (b) H3's 'SW Inv Cur Fault' adds the master 1.69 requirement. (c) H3's 'Bat Boost Fault' adds 'or The relay on the battery side of the inverter is not closed' plus master 1.69. (d) H3's 'HW Pv Cur Fault' adds 'Check whether PV positive and negative are connected'. (e) H3 REPLACES H1's 'Main Relay Open' + 'S1/S2/M1/M2 Close Fault' with a single 'Grid Relay Fault' reading 'The grid relay keeps open or close' - confirmed absent from the H3 text entirely. Never give an H3 owner the H1 remedy, or an H1 owner the H3 advice.

series.name: KH/KA (single-phase hybrid) - battery pack mismatch and pack hardware faults
series.notes: FoxESS's own remedy for every row in this block is the same single sentence, and on KH/KA it is worded differently from the hybrids: KH/KA prints 'Please contact our service department.' (verified 21 times in the KH/KA table, and the phrase 'contact battery supplier' appears ZERO times in either KH/KA copy) whereas H1 V1.6 and H3 V1.0.4 print 'Please contact battery supplier.' for the identical rows. So the KH/KA escalation route is FoxESS service, not the battery vendor - a real model-line difference, see CONFLICTS. The blocks below pair that instruction with the checks a technician CAN actually do at the pack before making that call. The 'Unmatch' family is the highest-incident group on Pakistani installs because packs are commonly bought in mixed batches over time. Verified on two independent official KH/KA copies. The CODE STRINGS are identical to the H1 V1.6 and H3 V1.0.4 tables but the REMEDY WORDING is not - see the note above and CONFLICTS item 15. The 12 Bms Volt/ChgCur/DchgCur/Temp/Relay/Sensor rows and the 'Bms Lost / Bms Ext Fault / Bms Int Fault' comms rows of the same table are covered under foxess-h1-ac1-g2-bms-comms and are NOT duplicated here.

series.name: KH/KA (single-phase hybrid) - parallel-system relay and sampling-consistency faults
series.notes: KH/KA models verified in the manual's own model list: KH7, KH8, KH9, KH9.9, KH10, KH10.5 and KA7, KA8, KA9, KA9.9, KA10, KA10.5. These rows exist ONLY on the KH/KA and H1/AC1 single-phase tables. The H3 text contains NONE of them - H3 collapses the whole grid-relay group into 'Grid Relay Fault' and omits the Cons Fault family entirely. FoxESS gives every code in this block the same bare 'Disconnect PV, grid and battery, then reconnect' remedy; the actions below are field practice built on the condition each row names. Confidence high because two INDEPENDENT official FoxESS copies (global AU-dated 2025-10-21 and AU V1.0.6) carry the table row-for-row identically.

series.name: R-Series / R G2 - LED indicator panel states (status, not faults)
series.notes: These are NOT fault codes - they are the four physical LEDs on the R-Series indicator panel (section 3.4) read as STATUS. All are isFault: false / severity: info. They are kept in their own series because a technician standing at a 75-110 kW unit with no app access diagnoses from these LEDs alone, and because the hybrids have no equivalent published LED table - the H1/KH-KA/H3 manuals mention the RED LED only in the single earth-fault note, and the T-Series has no LED status table at all. FoxESS's own threshold in the table is DC 200 V for the PV indicator. Verified identical in the PK V1.4 and RO R G2 V1.5 manuals.

series.name: R-Series / R G2 (three-phase grid-tie string) - grid voltage, frequency and current faults
series.notes: FORMAT WARNING: R-Series uses 4-DIGIT NUMERICS ONLY (1030, 1040, 1042 ...). There is no named-string namespace on this line - a Pakistani R/R G2 owner will never see 'Grid Volt Fault'. Models verified from the manual: R75, R100, R110, described by FoxESS as 'three-phase non-isolated grid-tied inverters' covering 75 kW to 110 kW, with 18 pairs of PV connectors on R75 and R100. R G2 V1.5 carries the identical table, which is what lifts this block to high confidence on two independent official sources. FoxESS's R remedies are longer and more procedural than the hybrid ones - they explicitly say to turn off AC and DC switches, WAIT 10 MINUTES, then turn them on in turn. That 10-minute wait appears nowhere in the hybrid manuals.

series.name: R-Series / R G2 (three-phase grid-tie string) - DC component, leakage, PV overcurrent, polarity and insulation faults
series.notes: R-Series DC and insulation block, still 4-DIGIT NUMERICS. FoxESS's R table uses a distinctive restart recipe that appears nowhere in the hybrid manuals: 'turn off the AC and DC side switches, wait for 10 minutes, and then turn on the AC and DC switches in turn to restart the inverter.' Two codes in this block break that pattern on purpose: 1035 is explicitly WEATHER-related ('excessive parasitic capacitance due to poor light or moist air. After the environment improves, the inverter will reconnect to the grid') and 1124 explicitly says to re-check on a better-weather day. Do not power-cycle a 1035 or 1124 in a storm. Confidence high: both codes appear identically in the PK V1.4 and RO R G2 V1.5 copies.

series.name: T-Series (single-phase grid-tie string) - AC leakage, insulation, ground and thermal faults
series.notes: The T-Series AC-safety and thermal block. 'ISO fault' here is a MEASURED IMPEDANCE test (FoxESS states 'Impedance should be >100kohm' and asks you to seek help if it IS >100kohm) - a completely different job from the hybrids' 'Iso Fault', which is an insulation-damage inspection with no measurement value. Likewise the T 'Ground fault' adds a PV DC switch-off step the hybrids' 'Ground Fault' does not. NEVER merge these with the hybrid insulation block. Note the T manual's separate section-6 note: it complies with IEC 62109-2 clause 13.9 and says an earth-fault alarm shows as 'Isolation fault' on screen with the RED LED lit. Confidence high: identical in both official FoxESS T copies.

series.name: T-Series (single-phase grid-tie string) - DC bus, PV input and memory faults
series.notes: The T-Series DC-side block. Every one of these codes has the SAME two-step FoxESS remedy: 'Disconnect PV (+), PV (-) using DC switch' then 'After the LCD switches off, reconnect and check again' - note that the T manual requires waiting for the LCD to actually go dark, which the hybrid manuals do not say. Do NOT merge with the hybrids' 'SW Bus Vol Fault' / 'DCI Fault' / 'Pv Volt Fault' strings: same physics, different vocabulary, and only the T rows carry the LCD-off wait. Confidence high: identical in both official FoxESS T copies (PK V1.0.1, global V1.0.2).

series.name: T-Series (single-phase grid-tie string) - grid and anti-islanding faults
series.notes: T-Series is NOT a hybrid - the manual contains no battery port and zero occurrences of the word 'battery'. Models verified from the manual's own list: T3-M, T4-M, T5-M, T6-M, T8-M, T10-M, T10-M-B, T12-M, T8(Dual)-M, T10(Dual)-M, T12(Dual)-M, T15-M, T17-M, T20-M, T23-M, T25-M, T30-M. FORMAT WARNING: these are short lowercase strings with spaces - 'Grid volt fault', NOT 'Grid Volt Fault'. Do NOT merge with foxess-h1-ac1-g2-grid even though the physics is identical, because FoxESS's own remedy text differs: T says 'Wait for one minute, grid may go back to normal working state' and 'Make sure that grid voltage and frequency complies with standards', whereas the hybrids say 'System will reconnect if the utility is back to normal'. Confidence high: two independent official FoxESS copies (PK V1.0.1 and global V1.0.2) carry all 22 rows and every remedy string identically.

brands.name: Fronius (AT)
brands.notes: Austrian Fronius International GmbH (Wels, AT). NOT Fronius (Pakistan) = the `fronus` brand in this KB; no Fronius Pakistan data was read or reused. No Fronius country setup or support channel for Pakistan could be found - PK presence not found.

series.name: GEN24 / Tauro / Verto grid-protection state codes
series.notes: Codes come from the Country Setup Menu manual's grid-protection tables. These are the 4-digit GEN24 codes; do NOT merge with the 3-digit Primo SnapINverter codes in SERIES 6-8 (e.g. 1114 GEN24 AC voltage too high vs 102 Primo AC voltage too high). State code 1082/1182 is an unresolved internal contradiction in the same manual (see CONFLICTS). Codes 1184/1185/1188/1189 are configuration-warning states, not faults. Where the same fault also appears in SERIES 2 (1030, 1173) the meaning is identical and is cross-referenced in notes.

series.name: GEN24 Primo 3.8-6.0 kW / Plus / SC - LED status indicator
series.notes: Operating LED rows (6) + Communication LED rows (4) = 10 unnumbered LED states. The GEN24 has no display; Fronius states 'in the event of faults, carry out the individual steps in the Fronius Solar.start app'. Codes are synthetic labels, NOT Fronius state-code numbers - do not match them numerically against SERIES 1. The manual's separate 'Sensor functions' block (1x AP open = blue flash, 2x WPS = green flash, 3 s message acknowledged = rapid white flash) describes the optical sensor, not an LED state row, and is recorded in notes rather than as entries. The Symo GEN24 equivalent table differs - see SERIES 6.

series.name: GEN24 Primo 3.8-6.0 kW / Plus / SC 208-240 (status code table)
series.notes: Single-phase GEN24 ('Primo') 3.8-6.0 kW plus the Plus and SC variants. Manual rev. 025 (manual 42,0426,0530). Unit type is on_grid_inverter; with a compatible battery connected (BAT switch position 1) the same unit also provides backup power, but Fronius's own product class and these state codes are grid-tied inverter codes. Codes here are shown on the inverter LED; the text says 'in the event of faults, carry out the individual steps in the Fronius Solar.start app'.

series.name: GEN24 support-page state codes (Primo GEN24 & Symo GEN24)
series.notes: Abridged list from the Fronius support page, kept separate from SERIES 1 (Country Setup manual) and SERIES 3 (Primo GEN24 operating instructions) even though 1030 and 1173 also appear there - the tables are independent and must not be merged. 994/995/996/997/999 are Solar.web communication state codes: Fronius groups them under one heading and does NOT publish a per-code description, so each is carried as low confidence. Manual versions: Fronius explicitly states the codes assume current firmware, so check the firmware before diagnosing.

series.name: GEN24 Symo 6-12 kW Plus / SC - LED status indicator
series.notes: Operating LED rows (6) + Communication LED rows (7) = 13 unnumbered LED states. Codes are synthetic LED labels, NOT Fronius state-code numbers. Differences vs SERIES 4 (Primo GEN24): the Symo Communication LED additionally shows blue = network connection active, '/ Flash blue' = update in progress, and white = service message present; and the yellow-flash Operating LED is worded 'The inverter displays an error. The inverter is operating correctly.' Do not merge this table with SERIES 4.

series.name: GEN24 Symo 6-12 kW Plus / SC (status code table)
series.notes: Three-phase GEN24 ('Symo') 6-10 kW Plus and 6-12 kW Plus SC. Manual rev. 033 (manual 42,0426,0315). The manual states status codes are shown in the user interface under System > Event Log, in the user menu under Notifications, and in Fronius Solar.web. Only 1030 is tabulated in this manual's status code chapter; the rest of the GEN24 state-code set is in SERIES 1 and SERIES 2. Fronius adds for this model line that a triggered surge protection device also switches the inverter off and produces 1030.

series.name: Fronius Primo 208-240 (SnapINverter) - Class 1 status codes
series.notes: SnapINverter Primo, legacy line, 3-digit codes on the inverter LCD (STATE 102 etc.). Fronius states these codes are 'typically temporary' and their cause lies in the grid: 'No device fault has occurred.' Behaviour and remedy text is identical for all seven codes in the published table. Primo Lite shares the Primo SnapINverter platform; Fronius publishes no separate Primo Lite state-code table (see NEGATIVE). Equivalent GEN24 4-digit equivalents: 102->1114, 103->1119, 105->1035, 106->1037, 112->1076, 107/108->1004.

series.name: Fronius Primo 208-240 (SnapINverter) - Class 3 status codes
series.notes: Legacy SnapINverter Primo, 3-digit codes, on-device LCD. Fronius: 'Class 3 comprises status codes that may appear during feed-in operation and that do not cause a permanent interruption of the grid power feed operation.' IMPORTANT per Fronius: codes 306 and 307 'appear naturally every morning and evening due to low solar irradiance. These status codes are not the result of a fault.' Codes 309 / 313 inherit the 308 behaviour and remedy block in the published table layout - flagged in their notes. Keep separate from the GEN24 4-digit tables.

brands.name: Fronus (PK)
brands.notes: Fronus Solar Energy (Wasiq Traders) — Pakistan ≠ Austrian Fronius (fronius.com). UAN 042-111-111-140, info@fronus.com, www.fronus.com. X1-Genki official manual = high (106 codes). X3 MIC = medium (cipher OCR). PV-2200/5200 image TS table = medium subset. Neo/Venus quarantine (SolaX).

series.name: Infineon Reborn (roadmap — covered under pv-hybrid codes)
series.notes: Infineon Reborn PV-2200 manual is the same product as pv-hybrid series (codes live in pv-hybrid.json). This file is a roadmap alias with zero duplicate codes to avoid double-counting.

series.name: Meta series (roadmap)
series.notes: ZERO codes — no Fronus-badged Meta fault table found in research pass. Gap documented.

series.name: Neo / Venus / Meta three-phase (SolaX-platform names) — quarantine
series.notes: QUARANTINE: downloaded Neo manual is SolaX-branded (solaxpower.com service contacts), no Fronus badge. Do not import SolaX named-fault list. x3genki10.pdf was the only Fronus Neo-adjacent file with no table.

series.name: PV-2200 / PV-5200 / Infineon Reborn (1.5–4.2KW hybrid)
series.notes: Image-only PDFs — troubleshooting table read via pdftoppm (p34 PV-5200). Subset of Voltronic-class codes (absence ≠ no such code). Medium (image read, single source). PV-2200 and PV-5200 share table family.

series.name: Sunny Island 3.0M / 4.4M / 6.0H / 8.0H
series.notes: Model scoping: doc SI30M-44M-60H-80H-BE-en-33W, the older 48 V Sunny Island family with a 3-digit display number that carries an F (Fault/error), W (Warning) or E (Event) prefix, plus a Level column 1-5. Slave variants add 'Slv1'/'Slv2'/'SL1'/'SL2' or 'S1'/'S2' to the same base number, meaning the same fault on a different cluster phase. series.name: Sunny Island X 30 / 50
series.notes: Model scoping: doc SIxx-20-BE-en-11 v1.1, the modern Sunny Island X backup inverter for PV + battery. The 4-digit event scheme here looks like Sunny Tripower's but the DC side is the BATTERY, not a PV string, so identical numbers mean different things: 3302 is a battery fault here but a PV shortfall on Sunny Tripower 3-6; 3501 says 'check battery and DC cabling' here but 'check generator' there; 3901/3902 are firmware/comms related here rather than 'DC start conditions'; 6501/6502/6509 are generic over-temperature and 6511 specifically names the choke area. The 9xxx block is battery-management events and the 10xxx block is internal battery-system events. Not to be merged with SERIES 3 (older Sunny Island 3.0M-8.0H, 3-digit F/W/E numbering).

series.name: Sunny Tripower 125
series.notes: Model scoping: doc STPxxx-70-BE-en-14 v1.4, 12 MPP trackers, 1500 V DC class central string inverter for industrial plants. Its event numbering is a SUPERSET of SERIES 1 but with real differences: this manual has DC overvoltage in the 34xx block (3401-3418) where SERIES 1 has nothing, a whole string-monitor block 40xx (4002, 4013-4024), AFCI events 4301 and 8204, and NO battery events. brands.notes: Ginlong Technologies brand, very common in Pakistan on-grid residential and small commercial. S5-GR1P single-phase string is the volume seller here; S5-EH1P-L hybrid is widely installed with 48V lithium.

series.name: EPM / export power manager, smart meter and CT (RS485 Modbus, zero-export)
series.notes: The EPM is not an inverter - it is the external export-limiting device that speaks RS485 Modbus to the inverters. Its codes are therefore filed in the official Solis library under the 20xx grid-connection / energy-storage block (2010/2011 Fail Safe, 201A CT_FAULT, 2019 MET_SEL_FAIL, 204B/204C G100 meter) and as message strings (RS485-all-fail, LimByEPM) rather than LCD hex alarms. Use this block when the fault is a meter, CT or export-limit problem, not an inverter problem. Positive real power (+kW) means EXPORT, negative (-kW) means IMPORT - get this backwards and you will chase a phantom fault.

series.name: RHI-(3-6)K-48ES-5G (single-phase hybrid + 48V battery)
series.notes: RHI is the 48 V single-phase hybrid line; the LCD prints TEXT names ONLY (no hex, no DATA field) - that is the difference from S5-EH1P-L / S6-EH1P-L which print 'NAME (10xx DATA:0000)'. The RHI table has its OWN battery-side rows (OV-Vbatt1, OV-Vbatt-H, Over-Load, OV-VBackup) that do not exist on the string-only on-grid tables. Do not merge with SERIES 4. Note the official EUR S5-EH1P(3-6)K-L(-BE) manual and the RHI manual share hardware and the same three-LED layout, but the LCD code format is still what differs, so they stay in separate blocks.

series.name: S5-EH1P(3-6)K-L (single-phase hybrid + 48V battery)
series.notes: SCOPE WARNING - read before merging anything into SERIES 1/2. On this platform the LCD prints NAME + hex + data field, e.g. 'OV-TEM (1032 DATA:0000)', and the SAME hex means a different thing: 1030 is GRID-INTF. = AC hardware overcurrent here (not grid interference); 1038 is 12Power-FAULT = 12V UNDERvoltage (not '12V supply fault'); 1052 is OV-ILLC = LLC hardware overcurrent (a BACKUP-side fault unique to hybrid). The official Solis alarm library files these rows under 'Only Energy Storage' with their own status-code column, which is why they are kept apart from the on-grid blocks.

series.name: S5-GC(25-50)K / S5-GC(50-60)K (three-phase commercial string 25-60kW, AFCI)

Only THREE LEDs on this model (POWER / OPERATION / ALARM) - no battery LED, no Bluetooth LED. This block is also the home of the on-grid-scope parallel and 3-phase communication codes (1060-106C) because the official Solis alarm library files them under 'Only Grid Connection'; the hybrid blocks keep their own 1060-106C rows with DIFFERENT names - see CONFLICTS.

series.notes: RS is the current-generation platform shared with SH (three-phase) and SG75/110/125CX-P2 (commercial). The manual states the table covers 'all PV inverters' and that 'only some of the faults may occur to the model you purchased' - so rows like 17 (Grid Voltage Imbalance), 323 (Grid Confrontation) and 75 (Parallel Communication) are PLATFORM-SHARED and will not appear on a single-phase SG2-6RS. Code numbering has NO leading zeros here (written '2, 3, 14, 15' not '002'). On this platform 2/3/14/15 are lumped into one generic 'Grid Overvoltage' row, NOT split into stage I/II like sungrow-sg. Ranges (System Fault, System Alarm) are documented as single rows and are recorded here as ranges, not expanded. Optimizer sub-device codes 4/512/1024 belong to the module-level optimizer, not the inverter.

series.name: SG2-8K G2 Premium (single-phase residential string 2-8kW)
series.notes: Codes are bare 3-digit integers on LCD/App, not E###. This is the older G2 Premium platform - it is the ONLY Sungrow line in this research that uses per-stage grid codes (002/015 = stage I/II over-voltage). Do NOT merge with sungrow-sg-rs (RS platform) or sungrow-sh: 002 means 'Grid over-voltage stage I' here but is grouped as a generic 'Grid Overvoltage' on RS/SH. 089 is a configuration warning, not a fault. Codes 501-514 are warning-class.

series.name: SH8.0RS / SH10RS (three-phase hybrid inverter with battery, 8-10kW)
series.notes: Shares the RS/CX platform code set with sungrow-sg-rs and sungrow-sg-cx-p2, so the string/meter/grid rows are IDENTICAL there.
